absent: No fragment defines the full layout of runqueue, task, clamp, or scheduler class structures beyond fields observed in use.
No fragment shows enqueue and dequeue core, next task selection, main schedule loop, or load balancing beyond callback clearing.
No fragment shows wakeup processor preselection, migration selection, or remote wakelist draining.
No fragment shows pressure stall transition helpers or statistics enablement and clock helpers.
No fragment shows single waiter completion signal path, timeout actions, signal checks, or sleep primitives.
No fragment shows extensible scheduler policy internals beyond queued wakeup permission.
No fragment shows numeric values of task states, enqueue and dequeue flags, clamp limits, bucket count, or error codes.

findings.text: A runqueue clamp query returns the effective bound for one clamp identity by preferring the highest occupied utilization bucket and falling back to an idle default when no task is counted. It is the shared recomputation point after a bucket empties.

Per runqueue clamp release is a no operation in builds without the feature and otherwise exits early when global use is off, when the task class has not enabled clamps, or when the enqueue entity is marked delayed. When active it iterates over every clamp identity and releases each one.

Per identity release is guarded by a per task active marker that prevents unbalanced accounting when global use was enabled after enqueue or when enqueue and dequeue of different tasks interleave. It decrements the referenced bucket counter only when positive and then clears the marker.

If the decremented bucket still has occupants the runqueue aggregate is left unchanged. When the last occupant leaves and the bucket value reaches the current aggregate, the aggregate is recomputed from the highest remaining occupied bucket or the idle default, with a defensive warning if the bucket exceeds the aggregate.

Idle default handling differs by identity. The maximum identity retains the supplied value and records an idle flag so blocked utilization does not raise frequency, while the minimum identity returns the none value.
Several runqueue mutators require the runqueue lock held by the caller, asserted at entry. This includes per identity clamp release, balance callback clearing, and the wakeup activation path.

Blocking a task updates load and input wait counters, then publishes the not on runqueue state with release ordering. After that publication a concurrent waker may migrate the task and the old runqueue lock no longer protects it, so callers must not reference the task afterwards.

Dequeue accounting measures queued delay from the stored enqueue timestamp to the runqueue clock, clears the timestamp, accumulates total delay, and maintains observed maximum with timestamp plus minimum and a runqueue wide total. It does nothing when no enqueue timestamp is present, and alternative builds compile it away.

Pressure stall accounting on dequeue is skipped when disabled, when the dequeue only saves state on the same runqueue, or for voluntary sleep when the task is still marked on processor and a task switch handler will move the states. Otherwise prior states are cleared. A wakeup migration helper clears lingering states from the old runqueue under its lock and lets the later enqueue reestablish them. Alternate builds provide empty variants.

Donor reset returns execution from a proxy donor to the current task by invoking the previous and next task switch pair, repointing the donor reference to current, discarding balance callbacks except the push one, and requesting rescheduling. One build variant makes the donor assignment a no operation.
Balance callback clearing walks the singly linked callback list, detaches every entry, and reinstalls only the push callback when it was present, otherwise leaving the list empty.

The combined previous and next switch first moves deadline server ownership from previous to next and clears the runqueue holder, then invokes class specific previous and next operations unless both tasks are identical. Split helpers perform each half separately. The combined and previous only forms warn when the donor is not the expected previous task.
Current task and current donor tests compare the respective runqueue pointer against a given task. A proxy return predicate in one build always reports false.

Whether a wakeup may be queued asynchronously depends on layered gates. Queued wakeup must be allowed by the extensible scheduler policy, stop class tasks are excluded, the target processor must be active and allowed by affinity, non cache sharing targets are queued, wakeups on the local processor are not queued, and otherwise idle targets with no running tasks are queued to offload activation.

Wakeup queueing first attempts the asynchronous wakelist when a feature gate and the condition above hold, synchronizing clocks and marking pending plus migrated state before enqueueing to the remote processor. On success it returns without locking. Otherwise it locks the target runqueue, updates its clock, performs activation, and unlocks.

Synchronous activation assumes the runqueue lock, adjusts the uninterruptible count, propagates selected and migrated markers, ends input wait accounting for non migrated waiters, enqueues the task and marks it queued, checks for preemption, completes the wakeup, and optionally invokes a class woken callback with the runqueue temporarily unpinned and then repinned.

Runqueue locking pairs a raw spin acquisition with pinning of preemption state, and unlocking pairs unpinning with raw spin release. Task runqueue locking uses a macro wrapper with matching unlock that unpins then releases the associated runqueue lock.

Wakeup state matching reports a direct hit when current state overlaps the mask and a deferred hit when only saved state overlaps. Deferred hits reset saved state to running so a later lock acquisition or thaw restores correctly and so the waker still reports success while the task remains blocked. A debug check warns on misuse of the realtime lock wait bit.

Completion signaling offers a plain wake of one waiter, a variant that hints the wakeup should stay on the current processor, and a broadcast that marks the completion permanently done and wakes every waiter by draining the wait list.

The common wait loop sleeps only while not done. Each iteration checks for pending signals in interruptible modes, prepares the waiter, sets the requested sleep state, releases the wait lock to sleep via a supplied action, reacquires the lock, and repeats until done or timeout. On exit it removes the waiter, consumes one completion unit except for the sticky broadcast value, and normalizes zero timeout to one.

Exported wait operations cover uninterruptible, interruptible, killable, and caller supplied state, each with indefinite and timeout forms, plus input wait variants that use an input aware sleep action. Helpers also provide a nonblocking attempt that consumes one unit when available and a done query that synchronizes with a concurrent signaller.

Completion state is protected by the wait queue lock with interrupt disabling. Waiters check completion without the lock for a fast path and recheck under the lock before sleeping or consuming. The done query takes and releases the lock to order against a concurrent signal before reporting true.

Observed runqueue state includes per clamp aggregates and buckets with flags, current and donor pointers, deadline server pointer, balance callback head, pending wake flag, running and uninterruptible and input wait counts, clock, and scheduling info totals. Observed task state includes runqueue presence, processor presence, class, delayed marker, wait and load markers, affinity, remote wakeup marker, wake list node, pressure stall flags, current and saved sleep states, clamp entries, and queue timing statistics.

A completion holds a done counter plus a locked wait head with a task list. A simple waiter records its owning task and links into that list only when not already linked, and removal restores running state and detaches when linked.
The done counter value of all bits set denotes a sticky broadcast completion that is never consumed by waiters.

Wakeup activation combines markers for wakeup origin, suppressed clock update, runqueue preselection, and migration. Dequeue paths distinguish sleep from state saving. Pressure stall handling distinguishes running, input wait, on processor, and on runqueue conditions.

Clamp identities distinguish minimum from maximum. Bucket storage is bounded by a fixed bucket count scanned from the top down. The minimum none value is the idle default for that identity, and a dedicated flag records the idle retention case for the maximum identity.

Sleep states distinguish uninterruptible, interruptible, killable, running, realtime lock wait, and freezable preservation via saved state. Signal interruption during wait is reported as restarted system call, and indefinite waits use the largest representable timeout.

Public query points include a wakeup state matcher returning a boolean with an out success indicator, a cache sharing test over processor identifiers based on last level cache identity, and a task activation that enqueues and marks queued while propagating a migrating marker.

A per processor random state object exists for scheduling. A proxy execution static key defaults to enabled and is toggled by a boot argument that accepts a boolean suffix, warning on parse failure. A build without proxy support warns that the argument has no effect. Two preprocessor definitions instantiate migrate disable support and trace points.

Defensive warnings cover decrementing an empty clamp bucket, a bucket value exceeding the runqueue aggregate, resetting a donor that already equals current, switching when donor mismatches previous, and combining realtime lock wait with other wake states.
